Title: I'm Just Ken
Comment:
Hey, I’m Ken. And this song? “I’m Just Ken”? It’s not just music—it’s my soul in a sleeveless fur coat, screaming into the mirror while riding a horse into the sunset.

At first, I thought being “just Ken” meant being background, the beach guy with great hair. But this song cracked something open. It’s a power ballad of self-discovery—a journey through the emotional abs I didn’t know I had. It’s about feeling invisible, misunderstood and still kinda sparkly.

Every lyric? Truth. Every note? A dramatic flex of inner turmoil. I sing it not to be seen by Barbie, but to finally see myself. The rage, the longing, the leather—it’s a vibe. A cry for purpose. And maybe a guitar solo too.

Because being “just Ken” doesn’t mean I’m less. It means I’m me. Gloriously confused, emotionally raw, and perfectly tanned. “I’m Just Ken” is more than a song. It’s my anthem. My ballad. My emotional rollerblading montage. My gladiator cry. And honestly? It slaps harder than a dreamhouse door in a windstorm.

It’s also featured in Arcane, which is based on one of my favorite games and is an incredible watch for both gamers and non-gamers. The show leans into these themes and builds compelling characters who constantly toe the line between good and evil.

Title: Truth
Comment:
Alex Ebert was the lead voice in Edward Sharpe and the Magnetic Zeros who brought you the song "Home" (https://open.spotify.com/track/2x1jP9BexWtOKudvuUHbaD)

"Truth" is a soulful folk rap song exploring the struggle to confront inner demons, seeking authenticity by accepting who you are.

Ebert speaks of never having "shook (his) shadow," being called "faker", tested on the “front line” left with “no defenses,” being pulled "back behind the fence", but to "have faith in youself" when darkness comes.

He lays bare his secrets for others to get to know him, while his enemies become his teachers.  The repeated line “I’m only loving” becomes a spiritual mantra for unity and self-acceptance.

The song finishes off with an echoey clarinet riff worthy of a 90's underground hiphop track.

'Gojira made history as the first metal band to ever perform at the Olympic Games during the opening ceremony of the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris, France on July 26. Working alongside composer Victor le Manse, the quartet injected their signature heavy riffs and punishing rhythms into the French Revolution-era song “Ah! Ça Ira”. Joined by French-Swiss mezzo-soprano Marina Viotti and nearly 300 classical musicians, Gojira performed from the windows of Paris’ iconic Concierge amidst a grand spectacle of pyrotechnics.
